back: Mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V, in kg m⁻³.
Normal force per unit area, p = F/A, in Pa (N m⁻²).
$\Delta p = \rho g \Delta h$; total pressure at depth $h$: $p_0 + \rho g h$.
The resultant upward force on an immersed object, caused by greater pressure on its lower surface than on its upper surface.
Upthrust $= \rho_{\text{fluid}} g V_{\text{displaced}}$ = weight of fluid displaced.
Upthrust = weight; fraction immersed = ρ_object / ρ_fluid.

front: Why does a hydrometer float lower in a less dense liquid?
back: It must displace a larger volume to get an upthrust equal to its weight.
Excess pressure $= \rho g \Delta h$, where $\Delta h$ is the difference in liquid levels.

front: Does upthrust on a submerged incompressible object change with depth?
back: No: the top and bottom pressures increase equally, so their difference is unchanged.
